title: Which button takes the lift from the Art Centre to the Sports Centre?
description: The lift in the building has its Art Centre on one floor and its Sports Centre higher up. The starting floor plus the movement gives the target floor, so the movement is the target floor take away the starting floor. Keeko's doubt is that the starting floor is taken away from the target floor the wrong way round.
teaching_notes: One idea: the button press is the movement needed, found as target floor take away starting floor. Watch for students who take the starting floor away from the target floor the wrong way round and get a button that moves the lift the wrong way.

source: Your starting floor is the Art Centre and your target floor
video_script.why: The child learns that the button press is the target floor take away the starting floor.
video_script.substitution: Use the book's own floors: the Art Centre at positive two and the Sports Centre at positive five.
video_script.anchor: the lift in {{NAME_10}}, from the Art Centre to the Sports Centre
video_script.wrong_answer: the starting floor take away the target floor
video_script.wrong_move: takes the target floor away from the starting floor, which gives a button that moves the lift away from the target
video_script.payoff_line: The button press is positive three.

names.{{NAME_3}}: the child at the Art Centre, floor positive two
names.{{NAME_5}}: the child at the Sports Centre, floor positive five
names.{{NAME_10}}: the building with floors above and below the ground

maths_rules: Starting floor + movement needed = target floor, so (+2) + ? = (+5)
movement needed = target floor - starting floor = (+5) - (+2) = +3
slip: (+2) - (+5) = -3 sends the lift down, away from floor +5
video_script.design: One lift, two floors, one rule. The rule is written first with a missing number, then solved by taking away.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; the lift shaft with the Art Centre at floor +2 and the Sports Centre at floor +5

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the lift shaft is drawn
marks.where: the Art Centre and the Sports Centre light up in turn
marks.ask: a lift button panel appears with a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the lift in {{NAME_10}}.
<bookmark mark='where'/>{{NAME_3}} is at the Art Centre, and {{NAME_5}} is at the Sports Centre.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>{{NAME_3}} wants to ride up to the Sports Centre. Which button should be pressed?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a button press moves the lift from the starting floor to the target floor; Starting floor + movement = Target floor

marks.press: an arrow shows the lift moving up and down on a button press
marks.move: the word movement is written beside the arrow
marks.rule: the line Starting floor + movement = Target floor is written

narration: <bookmark mark='press'/>Each button press moves the lift some floors, up or down.
<bookmark mark='move'/>How many floors the lift travels, and in which direction, is called the movement.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The starting floor plus the movement must give the target floor.

beats.on_screen: Given: starting floor = Art Centre = +2; target floor = Sports Centre = +5

marks.given: the two floors are written with their numbers

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the starting floor is the Art Centre, which is floor positive two.
The target floor is the Sports Centre, which is floor positive five.

beats.on_screen: To find: the button press (movement needed)

marks.find: the words button press are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the button press, which is the movement needed.

marks.rule: the rule is written in words
marks.fill: the floors replace the words and the movement stays a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, write the rule, starting floor plus movement needed equals target floor.
<bookmark mark='fill'/>Here, positive two plus a missing movement equals positive five.

beats.on_screen: Movement needed = target floor - starting floor = (+5) - (+2)

marks.sub: the rule turns into target floor take away starting floor
marks.vals: the two floors are put in: (+5) - (+2)

narration: <bookmark mark='sub'/>Step two, the movement is the target floor take away the starting floor.
<bookmark mark='vals'/>We write positive five take away positive two.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The button press is positive three.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Check it, positive two plus positive three lands on positive five.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: (+2) - (+5) = -3 crossed out; an arrow from floor +2 going down; floor +5 above

marks.down: an arrow shows the lift going down from floor +2
marks.fix: the expression is struck out and the target floor moves to the front

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the button is the starting floor take away the target floor.
<bookmark mark='down'/>That would be two take away five, which gives negative three, a button that sends the lift down.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the Sports Centre is above, so the target floor comes first, and the button is positive three.
